Since you’re considering a **Les Paul as an upgrade from your Strat**, try them side by side through the same amp if possible.

- **Try coil-splitting options.** Ask the staff to show you how the controls work, then compare the split sounds with the full humbuckers. See whether the extra tonal flexibility appeals to you.
- **Play in open D.** Ask to tune the guitar to D–A–D–F♯–A–D. Check how the strings feel and whether chords sound in tune up the neck.
- **Test fingerpicking.** Play a little of the “Blackbird” intro on a clean setting. Listen for clarity and see whether the neck and string height feel comfortable.
- **Check weight and comfort.** Try the Les Paul both seated and standing with a strap; it may feel heavier and differently shaped than your Strat.
- **Explore the pickups.** Compare the neck and bridge positions, and try the volume and tone controls at different settings.

Finally, ask about the setup and return policy. A comfortable, well-set-up guitar is worth prioritizing over one that just looks appealing.
